Q-2017-MID-P05-a.proof: Each Euclidean step preserves all common divisors; the last nonzero remainder is 1.

Q-2023S-MID-P06.proof: Direct integer division on the original two numbers gives valid nonnegative remainders 2^35-1, 2^30-1, 31, 0. This proves gcd=31 without any future modular theorem.

Q-2014-FINAL-P02-c.proof: For all positive a,n in the printed domain: a=qn+1, so every positive common divisor divides a-qn=1. Hence gcd(a,n)=1. This symbolic divisibility proof, rather than the sample check, proves the universal statement.

Q-2024S-MID-P12-a.proof: Put d=gcd(a,m)>0. Since a=du and m=dv, any integer combination ra+sm=d(ru+sv). If positive, the integer multiplier is at least 1, so the value is >=d. This holds for all positive a,m and all integer r,s.
Q-2024S-MID-P12-a.result: Every positive combination is at least gcd(a,m).

Q-2020-MID-P08.proof: The exact polynomial identity 3(14n+3)-2(21n+4)=1 has n coefficient 0 and constant 1. Every common divisor divides 1. This proves the result for all natural n (including either convention for zero).

Q-2018-MID-P05-a.proof: Bezout supplies s*y+t*z=1 because gcd(y,z)=1. Multiply by x: x=s*(x*y)+t*z*x. Both terms are divisible by z under the printed hypotheses, hence z divides x. Without coprimality this is not valid (x=1,y=z=2).

Q-2024S-MID-P12-b.proof: If an inverse b existed, a*b-m*k=1 would represent a positive integer 1 smaller than d=gcd(a,m)>1, contradicting the supplied original part (a). Equivalently every left term is divisible by d, so d would divide 1.

Q-2020-MID-P06.proof: Independent extended Euclid gives 17*53-5*180=1. All 180 standard representatives have been checked and only 17 multiplies 53 to residue 1.

Q-2017-MID-P05-b.proof: Independent Euclid gives inverse 59; full enumeration of 0..220 yields exactly 118. Substitution satisfies the original affine congruence. Coprimality proves all integer solutions are 118+221k; retain any printed standard-range restriction.

Q-2013-FINAL-P03.proof: For distinct standard representatives, 0<abs(x1-x2)<=pq-1<pq. Equal residues modulo distinct primes p,q would force pq to divide the difference, impossible. Thus distinct representatives differ in at least one residue (the contrapositive); given existence, this proves uniqueness. The official strict <pq-1 bound is a typo; <pq is sufficient.

Q-2019-FINAL-P02.proof: Pairwise gcds are 1. Independently calculated partial products [70, 45, 126], inverses [4, 5, 1], and raw sum 3298; exhaustive residue check gives only 148 modulo 630. CRT supplies exactly the full class 148+630k.

Q-2025F-FINAL-P06.proof: Pairwise gcds are 1. Independently calculated partial products [20, 15, 12], inverses [2, 3, 3], and raw sum 211; exhaustive residue check gives only 31 modulo 60. CRT supplies exactly the full class 31+60k. The original mod-2 equation is implied by mod-4=3, so it must be omitted before using the product theorem; period is 60, not 120.
